subsections.title: What the company actually does, in plain terms

blocks.text: Sika Interplant Systems Limited (SIKA) is a Bengaluru-based engineering company that describes itself as active in four areas: engineering (design and development); manufacturing, assembly and testing; projects and systems integration; and maintenance, repair and overhaul (MRO), with in-house capability "complemented by tie-ups with international partners". [F] (AR2026 p.26) The majority of the business serves the Aerospace, Defence & Space (AD&S) and Automotive sectors in India. [F] (AR2026 p.26) The screener profile adds interconnect solutions, electrical module integration and value-added distribution, and notes the company is a qualified Indian Offset Partner holding a defence production licence. [F] (SCREENER)

**The single most important disclosure in the annual report is that 68% of FY26 revenue was trading, not manufacturing.** Under the Ind AS 115 disaggregation, FY26 revenue of Rs 211.23 cr splits into Trading Rs 144.44 cr, Manufacturing Rs 65.07 cr and Services Rs 1.72 cr. [F] (AR2026 p.113) [E] That is 68.4% / 30.8% / 0.8%. [AI] An investor buying this as a pure defence-manufacturing franchise is buying a business whose revenue is predominantly the resale of bought-in product, and whose cost of material plus work-in-progress movement absorbed 69.4% of FY26 revenue. [E] (AR2026 p.92)

blocks.caption: How the revenue is actually made up, FY26 (Rs cr)

blocks.text: Geography: this is an almost entirely domestic revenue book funded by an import-heavy cost base. FY26 earnings in foreign exchange were Rs 1.55 cr (exports of goods Rs 1.25 cr, exports of services Rs 0.31 cr) against foreign-currency expenditure of Rs 91.94 cr, of which Rs 91.15 cr was stock-in-trade, raw materials and components. [F] (AR2026 p.19, p.102) [E] Exports were therefore 0.7% of revenue while foreign-currency purchases were 43.5% of revenue. [AI] The "export" line is immaterial; the meaningful currency exposure runs the other way.

End-market split by percentage is **not disclosed**. The company reports no segments at all: "The Company's operations predominantly consist of manufacturing/trading of Aerospace and Defence equipments and other sales does not contribute to 10% or more of the Company's total sales. Hence there are no reportable segments under Ind AS-108." [F] (AR2026 p.68) There is no split between defence, space, automotive or MRO anywhere in the report. [F] (AR2026 p.68) [AI] The class-of-goods note is the closest available proxy and it is not a segment disclosure: it gives no margins, no customers and no order backlog by line.

Customer profile is **not disclosed in any form**. No customer is named, no concentration percentage is given, and there is no top-1/top-5/top-10 disclosure anywhere in the annual report. [F] (AR2026 p.68, p.113) The only identifiable counterparties in the document are government bodies that have given the company awards or approvals - the Defence Research & Development Organisation, the Naval Physical & Oceanographic Laboratory, CEMILAC and DGAQA - and these are described as sources of recognition and certification, not as customers. [F] (AR2026 p.13, p.26)

Not disclosed is itself a finding. For a company capitalised at Rs 2,205 cr [F] (NUMBERS), the annual report contains no customer name, no customer concentration figure, no segment margin, no installed capacity, no utilisation rate, no export destination and no numeric guidance. [F] (AR2026 p.68, p.36) The company also states that it "does not have any presentations to institutional investors". [F] (AR2026 p.34) No earnings-call transcript was available in our evidence base.

subsections.title: Listing status and what it means for the evidence base

blocks.text: SIKA is not a recent listing. This is the 40th annual report; the company was incorporated with commercial production commencing on 20 December 1985 and carries CIN L29190KA1985PLC007363. [F] (AR2026 p.13, p.1) It is listed on BSE only, scrip code 523606, ISIN INE438E01032, with 100% of equity in dematerialised form. [F] (AR2026 p.34, p.36) There is no credit rating. [F] (AR2026 p.36) No prospectus or offer document was available in our evidence base, and none would be expected for a company listed this long.

items: The long listing history is a genuine positive: forty years of audited accounts, an unmodified audit opinion for FY26, and a ten-year statements series in our data. [F] (AR2026 p.40) [F] (NUMBERS)

But the evidence base is thin in the ways that matter for an equity thesis: single-exchange listing, no institutional presentations, no analyst calls, no investor deck, no order-book press releases in the available announcements. [F] (AR2026 p.34) [F] (ANNOUNCEMENTS)

Free float is small. Promoters hold 71.72%, unchanged across the last twelve quarters; FIIs 3.25% and DIIs 0.04% at Jun 2026. [F] (NUMBERS) Shareholder count rose from 7,502 at Mar 2024 to 26,959 at Jun 2026. [F] (NUMBERS) [AI] That pattern is consistent with a retail-driven re-rating rather than institutional accumulation.

The share capital is Rs 2 face value after a stock split referred to in the AGM notice; the split date is not disclosed in the documents available to us. [F] (AR2026 p.6) One note still describes the shares as "having a face value of Rs 10 each", which contradicts the balance sheet. [F] (AR2026 p.58)

blocks.text: Our variant perception is not that the business is bad - it is that the business being priced is not the business in the accounts. The market appears to be paying 63x trailing earnings and 11.85x trailing sales [F] (NUMBERS) for an indigenous defence-manufacturing compounder riding a Rs 7.85 lakh crore budget [F] (AR2026 p.27). What the FY26 accounts actually show is a 57-employee [F] (AR2026 p.33), single-site [F] (AR2026 p.36), predominantly trading [F] (AR2026 p.113) engineering intermediary with a shrinking order book [F] (AR2026 p.113), no disclosed customer [F] (AR2026 p.68), 43.5% of revenue spent in unhedged foreign currency [E] (AR2026 p.19, p.37), and roughly three-fifths of its balance sheet parked in debt mutual funds and undeveloped land [F] (AR2026 p.91). The operating business is real, well-certified and genuinely high-return on the capital it uses [F] (AR2026 p.26) [F] (NUMBERS) - but it is small, lumpy and now contracting, and at Rs 1,040 the share price sits above every fair value our model produces, including the bull case [F] (NUMBERS). The variant call is therefore about the gap between the narrative and the disclosure, not about whether the company is sound.

subsections.title: What the timeline reveals about how recent the current business really is

blocks.text: The corporate shell is forty years old but the business that supports today's valuation is about three years old. Sales were Rs 34 cr in FY17, Rs 98 cr in FY22, then fell to Rs 60 cr in FY23 before reaching Rs 211 cr in FY26. [F] (NUMBERS) The nine-year sales CAGR is 22.5% but the three-year CAGR is 52.1%. [F] (NUMBERS) [AI] Roughly 72% of FY26 revenue did not exist three years earlier, and the FY23 collapse - a 39% decline in a single year - demonstrates that this revenue base is capable of falling as fast as it rose.

The certification history also matters more than it first appears. The CEMILAC design approval, the credential most often cited for this kind of company, was held "from 1999 (until 2020 when such approvals were discontinued)". [F] (AR2026 p.13) The company still holds an Industrial Licence for defence production, DGAQA approval and AS9100. [F] (AR2026 p.26) [AI] That is a real but narrower moat than "continuously CEMILAC-approved since 1999" implies when read quickly.

A merger that created the Capital Reserve and Securities Premium is referenced with no date, counterparty or consideration [F] (AR2026 p.62), and 26,00,000 shares were "issued for consideration other than cash" with no explanation of when or to whom [F] (AR2026 p.54). Both are forty-year-old artefacts, but neither is explained in the current report.

sections.title: Business model: where the value is captured

subsections.title: The production and service chain, step by step

blocks.text: The company describes a four-stage capability set - engineering (design and development); manufacturing, assembly and testing; projects and systems integration; and MRO - and says its in-house capability is "complemented by tie-ups with international partners". [MC] (AR2026 p.26) Under long-gestation AD&S programmes it offers "a combination of one or more of design, development, manufacturing, assembly, testing, certification, supply and integration of systems, and implementation of the projects". [MC] (AR2026 p.26) The words "one or more of" are load-bearing: on any given contract the company may do only the last item on that list. [AI]

items: **Step 1 - Qualification.** The customer (typically a Ministry of Defence entity or a prime) qualifies the supplier. The company holds an Industrial Licence for defence production, DGAQA approval and AS9100 certification, and held CEMILAC design approval to 2020 [F] (AR2026 p.26)
**Step 2 - Order intake.** Orders are booked as a "contracted price". FY26 fresh and change orders were Rs 164.97 cr [F] (AR2026 p.113)

**Step 3 - Sourcing.** The dominant cost step. Cost of material, consumables and products was Rs 140.07 cr in FY26, of which Rs 91.15 cr was spent in foreign currency on stock-in-trade, raw materials and components [F] (AR2026 p.92, p.102)

**Step 4 - Manufacture, assembly and test.** Rs 65.07 cr of FY26 revenue was recognised as Manufacturing [F] (AR2026 p.113). Depreciation was Rs 1.05 cr on a net block of Rs 43.27 cr, of which Rs 33.45 cr is land [F] (AR2026 p.92, p.105)

**Step 5 - Integration, documentation and certification.** Management cites "established expertise in systems integration, documentation and certification" as the differentiator [MC] (AR2026 p.26). No revenue is separately attributed to it

**Step 6 - Delivery and revenue recognition.** Recognised "at the time of dispatch, delivery or upon formal customer acceptance depending on customer terms" - the auditor's single key audit matter [F] (AR2026 p.40)

**Step 7 - MRO and aftermarket.** Facilities set up for the company's own products and, "with the backing of its customers, with foreign partners", for foreign partners' AD&S products in India [MC] (AR2026 p.26). Services revenue was Rs 1.72 cr - 0.8% of the total [F] (AR2026 p.113). [AI] MRO is a narrative line, not yet a financial one

subsections.title: Where value is captured, and why

blocks.text: Value is captured in two places. First, in the qualification itself: a supplier approved onto an Indian defence programme faces limited re-tendering once the programme is running, which is what allows a Rs 211 cr revenue business to earn a 35% ROCE on a Rs 43 cr net block. [F] (NUMBERS) (AR2026 p.105) [AI] Second, and larger in rupee terms, in the spread between imported content and the price realised on Indian programmes: material and WIP cost absorbed 69.4% of FY26 revenue, leaving a 30.6% gross spread from which a Rs 10.25 cr wage bill and Rs 9.23 cr of other expenses were paid to reach a 21% EBITDA margin. [E] (AR2026 p.92) [F] (NUMBERS)

The economics of that second source are import-price and currency dependent, and the company carries the risk unhedged. [F] (AR2026 p.37) The gross spread narrowed in FY26 (69.4% cost ratio versus 67.3% in FY25) even as the EBITDA margin rose from 20% to 21%. blocks.text: **No.** The FY26 margin gain of 100bps came with a 210bp deterioration in the gross cost ratio. [F] (NUMBERS) With trailing revenue now 11.8% below FY26 and the Jun 2026 quarter down 37% year on year [F] (NUMBERS), the mechanism that lifted margins is the mechanism that will compress them.

The counter-argument, stated fairly: the TTM operating margin is 22%, the highest in the ten-year series, and the Jun 2026 quarter still delivered a 19.48% operating margin on a 37% revenue decline. [F] (NUMBERS) [AI] That is better cost behaviour than the FY23 analogue would predict, and it is consistent with a more variable cost base today (bought-in product) than in FY23. If that holds, the downside to margins is shallower than the FY23 precedent implies. It is one quarter of evidence.

subsections.title: The two questions the scores cannot answer

items: **First: is the approval moat customer-specific or programme-specific?** If SIKA is qualified with a small number of primes across many programmes, the moat is durable and the FY27 slowdown is timing. **Second: does the moat protect the Trading revenue or only the Manufacturing revenue?** If the certifications are what allow SIKA to be the approved channel for imported servo products and aircraft parts into Indian programmes, then 68.4% of revenue is moated and the economics are far better than they look. blocks.text: These two questions are, in our view, the entire investment case. A reader who can answer them - through channel checks, programme-level research or direct management access that this evidence base does not provide - would know whether to score this moat 3 or 7. **The moat is real, narrow and dependent on a single mechanism: government-granted qualification.** [AI] Defence approvals are genuinely hard to obtain, take years, and confer incumbency on live programmes - which is why a 57-person company with Rs 10 cr of operating hardware can earn a 35% ROCE. summary.one_line: A genuinely debt-free, 35%-ROCE, certification-backed Bengaluru aerospace and defence supplier whose accounts show a predominantly trading, import-dependent business with a shrinking order book and no customer disclosure - trading at a price that our reverse DCF says requires 77.6% annual sales growth for five years against a 15.6% base case, and above every fair value the model produces.
bull_points: Exceptional returns on a fortress balance sheet: ROCE 35% and ROE 25.8% in FY26, borrowings nil and debt/equity 0.00x for five consecutive years, with Rs 81 cr of investments plus Rs 27.58 cr of bank balances and cash against Rs 19.61 cr of total liabilities. [F] (NUMBERS) [F] (AR2026 p.91) [E]

Growth without capital: sales rose from Rs 60 cr (FY23) to Rs 211 cr (FY26), a 52.1% three-year CAGR, on cumulative three-year capex of Rs 11 cr - about Rs 13.7 of incremental revenue per rupee invested, with no capital work-in-progress since FY19. [F] (NUMBERS) [F] (AR2026 p.93) [E]

Real, government-granted entry barriers: an Industrial Licence for defence production, DGAQA approval, maintained AS9100 certification, a CSIR/DSIR-recognised R&D centre, and CEMILAC design approval held continuously from 1999 to 2020. [F] (AR2026 p.26)

A disclosed contracted order book of Rs 287.89 cr at 31 March 2026, equal to 1.36x FY26 revenue - the only hard forward number the company publishes, and it sits in a note management never discusses. [F] (AR2026 p.113) [E]

Directly evidenced policy tailwind: FY27 defence allocation up 15.2% to a record Rs 7.85 lakh cr, roughly 75% of the modernisation budget (~Rs 1.39 lakh cr) earmarked for domestic industry, global tenders barred below Rs 200 cr, and FY26 defence budget utilisation of ~99.6%. [F] (AR2026 p.27, p.28)
bear_points: The price embeds growth no scenario supports: the reverse DCF implies a 77.6% five-year sales CAGR against 15.6% in the base case, and all three scenario fair values - bear Rs 97.3, base Rs 170.3, bull Rs 239.3 - sit 90.6%, 83.6% and 77.0% below the Rs 1,040 price. No cell of the sensitivity grid exceeds Rs 225.1. [F] (NUMBERS)

The business is contracting now: order intake fell 39.0% to Rs 164.97 cr and closing backlog fell 13.9% in FY26 (book-to-bill 0.78x), Jun 2026 quarter sales fell 37.0% year on year, and TTM sales are 11.8% below FY26 after four consecutive sequential declines. [F] (AR2026 p.113) [F] (NUMBERS) [E]

It is more distributor than manufacturer: FY26 revenue was Trading Rs 144.44 cr (68.4%), Manufacturing Rs 65.07 cr (30.8%) and Services Rs 1.72 cr (0.8%), with Rs 91.15 cr of imported stock-in-trade and components (43.2% of revenue) and R&D of Rs 0.98 cr - while the most differentiated line, Aerospace systems, fell 36.3%. [F] (AR2026 p.113, p.102, p.76) [E]

Zero customer visibility and weak disclosure discipline: no customer named, no concentration figure, no reportable segments, no capacity or utilisation, no guidance, and no institutional presentations - alongside eighteen unreconciled figures in the annual report, including an MD&A ratio section that explains receivables and creditors as rising when both fell by roughly two-thirds. [F] (AR2026 p.68, p.36, p.34, p.29, p.30, p.91) [AI]

Margin gains are operating leverage, not structure, on an unhedged import base: the EBITDA margin rose 100bps to 21% in FY26 while the materials charge worsened 210bps to 69.4% of revenue, a Rs 1.63 cr net FX loss was absorbed, and management's claimed 'natural hedge' runs against a 59:1 import-to-export ratio. A 5% unrecovered input-cost shock alone takes the margin to 17.8%. [E] (AR2026 p.92, p.19, p.102) [MC] (AR2026 p.37)
watch_points: Q2 FY27 results, due by around mid-November 2026: does revenue recover above the year-ago Rs 51.58 cr, validating management's claim that Q1 FY27 was hit by 'supply-chain disruptions, delaying order execution and revenue recognition', or does the Rs 43 cr run rate persist?
